### BIT_AND

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/bitwise.rst

Computes the bitwise AND of two given numeric values. It can also be invoked directly using the `&` binary operator in SQL queries.

```APIDOC
## BIT_AND

### Description
Returns the bitwise AND of the given values. Also available as the `&` binary operator.

### Syntax
```sql
BIT_AND(expr1, expr2)
expr1 & expr2
```

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "i": [3, 10, 4, 8],
        "j": [4, 7, 9, 10],
    }
)
df.sql("""
    SELECT
      i,
      j,
      i & j AS i_bitand_op_j,
      BIT_AND(i, j) AS i_bitand_j
    FROM self
""")
```
```

### Dynamic group aggregation with negative every default offset (previous behavior)

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/releases/upgrade/1.md

Previous behavior where group_by_dynamic defaulted offset to negative every, starting the first window prior to the first timestamp.

```pycon
>>> from datetime import date
>>> df = pl.DataFrame({
...     "ts": [date(2020, 1, 1), date(2020, 1, 2), date(2020, 1, 3)],
...     "value": [1, 2, 3],
... })
>>> df.group_by_dynamic("ts", every="1d", period="2d").agg("value")
shape: (4, 2)
┌────────────┬───────────┐
│ ts         ┆ value     │
│ ---        ┆ ---       │
│ date       ┆ list[i64] │
╞════════════╪═══════════╡
│ 2019-12-31 ┆ [1]       │
│ 2020-01-01 ┆ [1, 2]    │
│ 2020-01-02 ┆ [2, 3]    │
│ 2020-01-03 ┆ [3]       │
└────────────┴───────────┘
```

### Select first row per group using DISTINCT ON

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/clauses.rst

Returns the first row for each unique combination of specified columns according to the given `ORDER BY`. Note that `DISTINCT ON` only supports column names, not arbitrary expressions.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "category": ["A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B"],
    "value": [30, 10, 20, 50, 40, 60],
    "label": ["x", "y", "z", "p", "q", "r"],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (category)
    category,
    value,
    label
  FROM self
  ORDER BY category, value DESC
""")
# shape: (2, 3)
# ┌──────────┬───────┬───────┐
# │ category ┆ value ┆ label │
# │ ---      ┆ ---   ┆ ---   │
# │ str      ┆ i64   ┆ str   │
# ╞══════════╪═══════╪═══════╡
# │ A        ┆ 30    ┆ x     │
# │ B        ┆ 60    ┆ r     │
# └──────────┴───────┴───────┘
```

### Query a DataFrame directly using DataFrame.sql referencing self

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/python_api.rst

Executes SQL directly against an underlying eager or lazy frame, referencing the frame as `self`. It returns a new frame of the same type representing the query result.

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "a": [1, 2, 3],
    "b": [4, 5, 6],
})
df.sql("""
  SELECT a::uint4, (b * b) AS bb
  FROM self WHERE a != 2
""")

# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ a   ┆ bb  │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ u32 ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 1   ┆ 16  │
# │ 3   ┆ 36  │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### EXCEPT BY NAME

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/set_operations.rst

Combines two SELECT statements and returns rows present in the first but not the second, matching columns by name rather than position. This permits differing column orders or counts between queries.

```APIDOC
## EXCEPT BY NAME

### Description
Combine the result sets of two SELECT statements, returning only the rows that appear in the first result set but not in the second, aligning columns by name instead of by ordinal position. This allows the two queries to have different column orders or different numbers of columns (only commonly-named columns are used for the comparison).

### Syntax
```sql
SELECT ... FROM table1
EXCEPT BY NAME
SELECT ... FROM table2
```

### Usage Example
```python
lf1 = pl.LazyFrame({
    "id": [1, 2, 3],
    "name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"],
})
lf2 = pl.LazyFrame({
    "name": ["Bob", "Charlie", "David"],
    "id": [2, 3, 4],
})
pl.sql("""
    SELECT * FROM lf1
    EXCEPT BY NAME
    SELECT * FROM lf2
""").sort(by="id").collect()
```
```

### BIT_OR

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/bitwise.rst

Computes the bitwise OR of two given numeric expressions. It can also be called using the `|` binary operator.

```APIDOC
## BIT_OR

### Description
Returns the bitwise OR of the given values. Also available as the `|` binary operator.

### Syntax
```sql
BIT_OR(expr1, expr2)
expr1 | expr2
```

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "i": [3, 10, 4, 8],
        "j": [4, 7, 9, 10],
    }
)
df.sql("""
    SELECT
      i,
      j,
      i | j AS i_bitor_op_j,
      BIT_OR(i, j) AS i_bitor_j
    FROM self
""")
```
```

### NULLIF

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/conditional.rst

Returns NULL if two expressions are equal, otherwise returns the first expression value. Useful for conditional data cleansing and handling sentinel values.

```APIDOC
## NULLIF

### Description
Returns NULL if two expressions are equal, otherwise returns the first.

### Syntax
```sql
NULLIF(expr1, expr2)
```

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": [100, 200, 300, 400],
    "bar": [20, 10, 30, 40]
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT NULLIF(foo, bar) AS baz FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ baz │
# │ --- │
# │ i64 │
# ╞═════╡
# │ 100 │
# │ 200 │
# │ 300 │
# │ 400 │
# └─────┘
```
```

### Create Polars expressions from SQL fragments with pl.sql_expr

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/python_api.rst

Use `polars.sql_expr()` to generate native Polars expressions from SQL syntax fragments, suitable for functions like `with_columns`.

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "a": [1, 2, 3],
    "b": [4, 5, 6],
})
df.with_columns(
    pl.sql_expr("(a * a) + (b::float / 2) AS expr1"),
    pl.sql_expr("CONCAT_WS(':',a,b) AS expr2")
)

# shape: (3, 4)
# ┌─────┬─────┬───────┬───────┐
# │ a   ┆ b   ┆ expr1 ┆ expr2 │
# │ --- ┆ --- ┆ ---   ┆ ---   │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 ┆ f64   ┆ str   │
# ╞═════╪═════╪═══════╪═══════╡
# │ 1   ┆ 4   ┆ 3.0   ┆ 1:4   │
# │ 2   ┆ 5   ┆ 6.5   ┆ 2:5   │
# │ 3   ┆ 6   ┆ 12.0  ┆ 3:6   │
# └─────┴─────┴───────┴───────┘
```

### Compute cosine in degrees with COSD

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/trigonometry.rst

Calculate the cosine of values specified in degrees in a Polars SQL query.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"degs": [0, 45, 180, 225]})
df.sql("SELECT degs, COSD(degs) AS cosd FROM self")
# shape: (4, 2)
# ┌──────┬───────────┐
# │ degs ┆ cosd      │
# │ ---  ┆ ---       │
# │ i64  ┆ f64       │
# ╞══════╪═══════════╡
# │ 0    ┆ 1.0       │
# │ 45   ┆ 0.707107  │
# │ 180  ┆ -1.0      │
# │ 225  ┆ -0.707107 │
# └──────┴───────────┘
```

### UNION BY NAME

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/set_operations.rst

Combines the result sets of two or more SELECT statements by aligning columns by name rather than by ordinal position. When ALL is omitted, duplicate rows are removed from the final result.

```APIDOC
## UNION BY NAME

### Description
Combine the result sets of two or more SELECT statements, aligning columns by name instead of by ordinal position; if `ALL` is omitted the final result will have no duplicate rows. This also combines columns from both datasets.

### Example
```python
pl.sql("""
    SELECT * FROM lf1
    UNION BY NAME
    SELECT * FROM lf2
""").sort(by="id").collect()
# shape: (6, 3)
# ┌─────┬─────────┬──────┐
# │ id  ┆ name    ┆ age  │
# │ --- ┆ ---     ┆ ---  │
# │ i64 ┆ str     ┆ i64  │
# ╞═════╪═════════╪══════╡
# │ 1   ┆ Alice   ┆ null │
# │ 2   ┆ Bob     ┆ null │
# │ 2   ┆ Bob     ┆ 30   │
# │ 3   ┆ Charlie ┆ 25   │
# │ 3   ┆ Charlie ┆ null │
# │ 4   ┆ David   ┆ 45   │
# └─────┴─────────┴──────┘
```
```

### Implement compute kernels and expression dispatch in Rust

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/development/contributing/code-style.md

Demonstrates how to write performant kernels closest to Arrow arrays, handle validities, align ChunkedArrays, and dispatch numeric series.

```rust
use std::ops::Add;

use polars::export::arrow::array::*;
use polars::export::arrow::compute::arity::binary;
use polars::export::arrow::types::NativeType;
use polars::prelude::*;
use polars_core::utils::{align_chunks_binary, combine_validities_and};
use polars_core::with_match_physical_numeric_polars_type;

// Prefer to do the compute closest to the arrow arrays.
// this will tend to be faster as iterators can work directly on slices and don't have
// to go through boxed traits
fn compute_kernel<T>(arr_1: &PrimitiveArray<T>, arr_2: &PrimitiveArray<T>) -> PrimitiveArray<T>
where
    T: Add<Output = T> + NativeType,
{
    // process the null data separately
    // this saves an expensive branch and bitoperation when iterating
    let validity_1 = arr_1.validity();
    let validity_2 = arr_2.validity();

    let validity = combine_validities_and(validity_1, validity_2);

    // process the numerical data as if there were no validities
    let values_1: &[T] = arr_1.values().as_slice();
    let values_2: &[T] = arr_2.values().as_slice();

    let values = values_1
        .iter()
        .zip(values_2)
        .map(|(a, b)| *a + *b)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();

    PrimitiveArray::from_data_default(values.into(), validity)
}

// Same kernel as above, but uses the `binary` abstraction. Prefer this,
#[allow(dead_code)]
fn compute_kernel2<T>(arr_1: &PrimitiveArray<T>, arr_2: &PrimitiveArray<T>) -> PrimitiveArray<T>
where
    T: Add<Output = T> + NativeType,
{
    binary(arr_1, arr_2, arr_1.dtype().clone(), |a, b| a + b)
}

fn compute_chunked_array_2_args<T: PolarsNumericType>(
    ca_1: &ChunkedArray<T>,
    ca_2: &ChunkedArray<T>,
) -> ChunkedArray<T> {
    // This ensures both ChunkedArrays have the same number of chunks with the
    // same offset and the same length.
    let (ca_1, ca_2) = align_chunks_binary(ca_1, ca_2);
    let chunks = ca_1
        .downcast_iter()
        .zip(ca_2.downcast_iter())
        .map(|(arr_1, arr_2)| compute_kernel(arr_1, arr_2));
    ChunkedArray::from_chunk_iter(ca_1.name(), chunks)
}

pub fn compute_expr_2_args(arg_1: &Series, arg_2: &Series) -> Series {
    // Dispatch the numerical series to `compute_chunked_array_2_args`.
    with_match_physical_numeric_polars_type!(arg_1.dtype(), |$T| {
        let ca_1: &ChunkedArray<$T> = arg_1.as_ref().as_ref().as_ref();
        let ca_2: &ChunkedArray<$T> = arg_2.as_ref().as_ref().as_ref();
        compute_chunked_array_2_args(ca_1, ca_2).into_series()
    })
}
```

### Compute bitwise OR using BIT_OR and the | operator

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/bitwise.rst

Performs a bitwise OR operation on two integer columns using both the BIT_OR function and the | binary operator.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
      "i": [3, 10, 4, 8],
      "j": [4, 7, 9, 10],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    i,
    j,
    i | j AS i_bitor_op_j,
    BIT_OR(i, j) AS i_bitor_j
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 4)
# ┌─────┬─────┬──────────────┬───────────┐
# │ i   ┆ j   ┆ i_bitor_op_j ┆ i_bitor_j │
# │ --- ┆ --- ┆ ---          ┆ ---       │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 ┆ i64          ┆ i64       │
# ╞═════╪═════╪══════════════╪═══════════╡
# │ 3   ┆ 4   ┆ 7            ┆ 7         │
# │ 10  ┆ 7   ┆ 15           ┆ 15        │
# │ 4   ┆ 9   ┆ 13           ┆ 13        │
# │ 8   ┆ 10  ┆ 10           ┆ 10        │
# └─────┴─────┴──────────────┴───────────┘
```

### LPAD

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Pads a string on the left to a specified target length with an optional fill character. If the string exceeds the specified length, it is truncated.

```APIDOC
### Syntax

```sql
LPAD(string, length [, fill])
```

### Description

Pads a string on the left to a specified length using an optional fill character (default is a space). If the string is longer than the target length it is truncated.

### Example

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["hello", "hi", "a", None, "longstr"]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    foo,
    LPAD(foo, 7) AS lpad,
    LPAD(foo, 7, 'x') AS lpad_x,
    LPAD(foo, 4, '#') AS lpad_trunc
  FROM self
""")
```

### Compute bitwise AND using BIT_AND and the & operator

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/bitwise.rst

Calculates the bitwise AND of two integer columns using both the BIT_AND function and the & binary operator in Polars SQL.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
      "i": [3, 10, 4, 8],
      "j": [4, 7, 9, 10],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    i,
    j,
    i & j AS i_bitand_op_j,
    BIT_AND(i, j) AS i_bitand_j
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 4)
# ┌─────┬─────┬───────────────┬────────────┐
# │ i   ┆ j   ┆ i_bitand_op_j ┆ i_bitand_j │
# │ --- ┆ --- ┆ ---           ┆ ---        │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 ┆ i64           ┆ i64        │
# ╞═════╪═════╪═══════════════╪════════════╡
# │ 3   ┆ 4   ┆ 0             ┆ 0          │
# │ 10  ┆ 7   ┆ 2             ┆ 2          │
# │ 4   ┆ 9   ┆ 0             ┆ 0          │
# │ 8   ┆ 10  ┆ 8             ┆ 8          │
# └─────┴─────┴───────────────┴────────────┘
```

### UNNEST

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/array.rst

Unnest or explode an array column into multiple rows within a Polars SQL query.

```APIDOC
## UNNEST

### Description
Unnest/explode an array column into multiple rows.

### Syntax
```sql
UNNEST(column)
```

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": [["a", "b", "c"], ["d", "e"]],
    "bar": [[6, 7, 8], [9, 10]]
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    UNNEST(foo) AS f,
    UNNEST(bar) AS b
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (5, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ f   ┆ b   │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ str ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ a   ┆ 6   │
# │ b   ┆ 7   │
# │ c   ┆ 8   │
# │ d   ┆ 9   │

### Define custom composite strategies for nested list columns

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/testing.rst

Creates a Hypothesis composite strategy for List[UInt8] types generating ordered pairs of integer values within DataFrames of fixed size.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars.testing.parametric import column, dataframes, lists

import hypothesis.strategies as st
from hypothesis import given

@st.composite
def uint8_pairs(draw: st.DrawFn):
    uints = lists(pl.UInt8, size=2)
    pairs = list(zip(draw(uints), draw(uints)))
    return [sorted(ints) for ints in pairs]

@given(
    dataframes(
        cols=[
            column("colx", strategy=uint8_pairs()),
            column("coly", strategy=uint8_pairs()),
            column("colz", strategy=uint8_pairs()),
        ],
        min_size=3,
        max_size=3,
    )
)
def test_miscellaneous(df: pl.DataFrame): ...

    # Example frame:
    # ┌─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
    # │ colx                    ┆ coly                    ┆ colz                     │
    # │ ---                     ┆ ---                     ┆ ---                      │
    # │ list[list[i64]]         ┆ list[list[i64]]         ┆ list[list[i64]]          │
    # ╞═════════════════════════╪═════════════════════════╪══════════════════════════╡
    # │ [[143, 235], [75, 101]] ┆ [[143, 235], [75, 101]] ┆ [[31, 41], [57, 250]]    │
    # │ [[87, 186], [174, 179]] ┆ [[87, 186], [174, 179]] ┆ [[112, 213], [149, 221]] │
    # │ [[23, 85], [7, 86]]     ┆ [[23, 85], [7, 86]]     ┆ [[22, 255], [27, 28]]    │
    # └─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

### Limit returned rows with ANSI standard FETCH clause

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/clauses.rst

ANSI SQL standard alternative to LIMIT for row restrictions that can be combined with OFFSET. Note that WITH TIES and PERCENT modifiers are not currently supported.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": ["b", "a", "c", "b"],
    "bar": [20, 10, 40, 30],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT foo, bar
  FROM self
  ORDER BY bar
  OFFSET 1 FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY
""")
# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ foo ┆ bar │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ str ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ b   ┆ 20  │
# │ b   ┆ 30  │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### Perform column-aligned set difference with EXCEPT BY NAME

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/set_operations.rst

Returns rows appearing in the first result set but not the second, aligning columns by name rather than position. Queries can have differing column orders or counts, using only common columns for comparison.

```python
lf1 = pl.LazyFrame({
    "id": [1, 2, 3],
    "name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"],
})
lf2 = pl.LazyFrame({
    "name": ["Bob", "Charlie", "David"],
    "id": [2, 3, 4],
})
pl.sql("""
    SELECT * FROM lf1
    EXCEPT BY NAME
    SELECT * FROM lf2
""").sort(by="id").collect()
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌─────┬───────┐
# │ id  ┆ name  │
# │ --- ┆ ---   │
# │ i64 ┆ str   │
# ╞═════╪═══════╡
# │ 1   ┆ Alice │
# └─────┴───────┘
```

### Skip rows with OFFSET clause

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/clauses.rst

Skip a specified number of rows before returning query results. Can be combined with LIMIT to paginate data.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": ["b", "a", "c", "b"],
    "bar": [20, 10, 40, 30],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT foo, bar FROM self LIMIT 2 OFFSET 2
""")
# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ foo ┆ bar │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ str ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ c   ┆ 40  │
# │ b   ┆ 30  │
# └─────┴─────┘

### Simulate GPU fallback PerformanceWarning output

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/gpu-support.md

Prints the expected PerformanceWarning and error message format emitted when GPU execution encounters an unsupported operation.

```python
--8<-- "python/user-guide/lazy/gpu.py:fallback-setup"
print(
    "PerformanceWarning: Query execution with GPU not possible: unsupported operations"
)
print("The errors were:")
print("- NotImplementedError: dtype=Binary conversion not supported")
print("  return wrap_df(ldf.collect(engine, callback))")
print()
print(q.collect())
```

### Convert datatypes safely using TRY_CAST

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/types.rst

Convert column values to target datatypes, returning NULL instead of raising an error when a conversion fails.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": [65432, 10101, -33333],
    "bar": ["1999-12-31", "N/A", "2024-01-01"],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    TRY_CAST(foo AS uint2),
    TRY_CAST(bar AS date)
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (3, 2)
# ┌───────┬────────────┐
# │ foo   ┆ bar        │
# │ ---   ┆ ---        │
# │ u16   ┆ date       │
# ╞═══════╪════════════╡
# │ 65432 ┆ 1999-12-31 │
# │ 10101 ┆ null       │
# │ null  ┆ 2024-01-01 │
# └───────┴────────────┘
```

### expr.meta

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/expressions/meta.rst

Namespace attribute on Polars expressions providing operations to inspect, compare, or modify expressions directly rather than evaluating them on data.

```APIDOC
## expr.meta

### Description
Operations available under the `expr.meta` attribute allow modifying expressions or checking equality of expressions directly instead of evaluating them against data. Useful for deduplicating or inspecting expressions.

### Methods & Attributes Documented
- `expr.meta` - Access metadata interface on an expression for comparisons or hashing
- `meta.as_expression()` - Converts a meta expression back into a standard Polars expression

### Usage Example
```python
a1 = pl.col("a")
a2 = pl.col("a")
b1 = pl.col("b") + 1
b2 = pl.col("b") + 2
b3 = pl.col("b") + 2

# Create a set of meta expressions to deduplicate
s = {e.meta for e in [a1, a2, b1, b2, b3]}
assert len(s) == 3

# Turn back into expressions to get the final unique expressions
unique_expressions = [e.as_expression() for e in s]
```
```

### Combine multiple Polars window functions across different groups

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/migration/pandas.md

Applies multiple window expressions within a single with_columns call. Polars caches window expressions applied over the same group for optimal performance.

```python
df.with_columns(
    pl.col("c").count().over("c").alias("size"),
    pl.col("c").sum().over("type").alias("sum"),
    pl.col("type").reverse().over("c").alias("reverse_type")
)
```

```text
shape: (7, 5)
┌─────┬──────┬──────┬─────┬──────────────┐
│ c   ┆ type ┆ size ┆ sum ┆ reverse_type │
│ --- ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ --- ┆ ---          │
│ i64 ┆ str  ┆ u32  ┆ i64 ┆ str          │
╞═════╪══════╪══════╪═════╪══════════════╡
│ 1   ┆ m    ┆ 3    ┆ 5   ┆ o            │
│ 1   ┆ n    ┆ 3    ┆ 5   ┆ n            │
│ 1   ┆ o    ┆ 3    ┆ 1   ┆ m            │
│ 2   ┆ m    ┆ 4    ┆ 5   ┆ n            │
│ 2   ┆ m    ┆ 4    ┆ 5   ┆ n            │
│ 2   ┆ n    ┆ 4    ┆ 5   ┆ m            │
│ 2   ┆ n    ┆ 4    ┆ 5   ┆ m            │
└─────┴──────┴──────┴─────┴──────────────┘
```

### Use COALESCE to return first non-null value

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/conditional.rst

Evaluates expressions in order and returns the first non-null value across the provided columns.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": [1, None, 3, None],
    "bar": [1, 2, None, 4],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT foo, bar, COALESCE(foo, bar) AS baz FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 3)
# ┌──────┬──────┬─────┐
# │ foo  ┆ bar  ┆ baz │
# │ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ --- │
# │ i64  ┆ i64  ┆ i64 │
# ╞══════╪══════╪═════╡
# │ 1    ┆ 1    ┆ 1   │
# │ null ┆ 2    ┆ 2   │
# │ 3    ┆ null ┆ 3   │
# │ null ┆ 4    ┆ 4   │
# └──────┴──────┴─────┘

### Use IFNULL to provide fallback values for NULL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/conditional.rst

Replaces NULL values in an expression with a designated alternative fallback value.

```python

  {

  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT IFNULL(foo, 'n/a') AS baz FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ baz │
# │ --- │
# │ str │
# ╞═════╡
# │ a   │
# │ n/a │
# │ n/a │
# │ d   │
# └─────┘
```

### Unnest array columns into multiple rows using UNNEST in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/array.rst

Explodes array columns into multiple rows using the UNNEST SQL function directly on a DataFrame.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": [["a", "b", "c"], ["d", "e"]],
    "bar": [[6, 7, 8], [9, 10]]
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    UNNEST(foo) AS f,
    UNNEST(bar) AS b
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (5, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ f   ┆ b   │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ str ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ a   ┆ 6   │
# │ b   ┆ 7   │
# │ c   ┆ 8   │
# │ d   ┆ 9   │
# │ e   ┆ 10  │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### LEAST

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/conditional.rst

Returns the smallest value across a list of expressions in Polars SQL. Useful for element-wise minimum comparisons across multiple columns or expressions.

```APIDOC
## LEAST

### Description
Returns the smallest value in the list of expressions.

### Syntax
```sql
LEAST(expr1, expr2, ...)
```

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": [100, 200, 300, 400],
    "bar": [20, 10, 30, 40]
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT LEAST(foo, bar) AS baz FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ baz │
# │ --- │
# │ i64 │
# ╞═════╡
# │ 20  │
# │ 10  │
# │ 30  │
# │ 40  │
# └─────┘
```
```

### Execute diverging queries with collect_all

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/lazy/execution.md

Use `pl.collect_all` when multiple downstream `LazyFrame` branches originate from a shared expensive query plan to ensure the base query executes only once.

```python
# Some expensive LazyFrame
lf: LazyFrame

lf_1 = lf.select(pl.all().sum())

lf_2 = lf.some_other_computation()

pl.collect_all([lf_1, lf_2]) # this will execute lf only once!
```

### Split strings into arrays with STRING_TO_ARRAY

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Splits a string by a delimiter into an array of strings in Polars SQL.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["aa,bb,cc", "x,y"]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT foo, STRING_TO_ARRAY(foo, ',') AS arr FROM self
""")
# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌──────────┬────────────────────┐
# │ foo      ┆ arr                │
# │ ---      ┆ ---                │
# │ str      ┆ list[str]          │
# ╞══════════╪════════════════════╡
# │ aa,bb,cc ┆ ["aa", "bb", "cc"] │
# │ x,y      ┆ ["x", "y"]         │
# └──────────┴────────────────────┘
```

### Match regex using ~ and !~ operators

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/operators/index.rst

Use `~` to filter rows where a column matches a regular expression and `!~` to filter rows where it does not.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"idx": [0, 1, 2, 3], "lbl": ["foo", "bar", "baz", "zap"]})
df.sql("SELECT * FROM self WHERE lbl ~ '.*[aeiou]$'")
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ idx ┆ lbl │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ str │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 0   ┆ foo │
# └─────┴─────┘

df.sql("SELECT * FROM self WHERE lbl !~ '^b[aeiou]'")
# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ idx ┆ lbl │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ str │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 0   ┆ foo │
# │ 3   ┆ zap │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### Combine queries with UNION BY NAME in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/set_operations.rst

Combines the result sets of two SELECT statements by aligning columns by name. Omitting ALL removes duplicate rows from the final result and combines columns from both datasets.

```python
pl.sql("""
    SELECT * FROM lf1
    UNION BY NAME
    SELECT * FROM lf2
""").sort(by="id").collect()
# shape: (6, 3)
# ┌─────┬─────────┬──────┐
# │ id  ┆ name    ┆ age  │
# │ --- ┆ ---     ┆ ---  │
# │ i64 ┆ str     ┆ i64  │
# ╞═════╪═════════╪══════╡
# │ 1   ┆ Alice   ┆ null │
# │ 2   ┆ Bob     ┆ null │
# │ 2   ┆ Bob     ┆ 30   │
# │ 3   ┆ Charlie ┆ 25   │
# │ 3   ┆ Charlie ┆ null │
# │ 4   ┆ David   ┆ 45   │
# └─────┴─────────┴──────┘
```

with pl.Config() as cfg:

### Compute bitwise XOR using BIT_XOR and the XOR operator

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/bitwise.rst

Executes a bitwise XOR on two integer columns using both the BIT_XOR function and the XOR binary operator.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
      "i": [3, 10, 4, 8],
      "j": [4, 7, 9, 10],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    i,
    j,
    i XOR j AS i_bitxor_op_j,
    BIT_XOR(i, j) AS i_bitxor_j
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 4)
# ┌─────┬─────┬───────────────┬────────────┐
# │ i   ┆ j   ┆ i_bitxor_op_j ┆ i_bitxor_j │
# │ --- ┆ --- ┆ ---           ┆ ---        │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 ┆ i64           ┆ i64        │
# ╞═════╪═════╪═══════════════╪════════════╡
# │ 3   ┆ 4   ┆ 7             ┆ 7          │
# │ 10  ┆ 7   ┆ 13            ┆ 13         │
# │ 4   ┆ 9   ┆ 13            ┆ 13         │
# │ 8   ┆ 10  ┆ 2             ┆ 2          │
# └─────┴─────┴───────────────┴────────────┘
```

### Perform set difference with EXCEPT

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/set_operations.rst

Combines the result sets of two SELECT statements and returns only the rows appearing in the first result set but not in the second.

```python
lf1 = pl.LazyFrame({
    "id": [1, 2, 3],
    "name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"],
})
lf2 = pl.LazyFrame({
    "id": [2, 3, 4],
    "age": [30, 25, 45],
    "name": ["Bob", "Charlie", "David"],
})
pl.sql("""
    SELECT id, name FROM lf1
    EXCEPT
    SELECT id, name FROM lf2
""").sort(by="id").collect()
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌─────┬───────┐
# │ id  ┆ name  │
# │ --- ┆ ---   │
# │ i64 ┆ str   │
# ╞═════╪═══════╡
# │ 1   ┆ Alice │
# └─────┴───────┘
```

### ATAN(col)

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/trigonometry.rst

Computes the inverse tangent (arctangent) of the input column in radians. This function is invoked directly in Polars SQL expressions.

```APIDOC
## ATAN

### Description
Compute inverse tangent of the input column (in radians).

### Syntax
```sql
ATAN(column)
```

### Parameters
- **column** (numeric) - Input column or numeric expression in radians.

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"rads": [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0]})
df.sql("SELECT rads, ATAN(rads) AS atan FROM self")
# shape: (4, 2)
# ┌──────┬───────────┐
# │ rads ┆ atan      │
# │ ---  ┆ ---       │
# │ f64  ┆ f64       │
# ╞══════╪═══════════╡
# │ -1.0 ┆ -0.785398 │
# │ 0.0  ┆ 0.0       │
# │ 1.0  ┆ 0.785398  │
# │ 2.0  ┆ 1.107149  │
# └──────┴───────────┘
```
```

### Import and use Polars selectors in DataFrame operations

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/selectors.rst

Import `polars.selectors` as `cs` to select columns by type in operations such as `group_by` and aggregation.

```python
import polars.selectors as cs
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "w": ["xx", "yy", "xx", "yy", "xx"],
        "x": [1, 2, 1, 4, -2],
        "y": [3.0, 4.5, 1.0, 2.5, -2.0],
        "z": ["a", "b", "a", "b", "b"],
    },
)
df.group_by(cs.string()).agg(cs.numeric().sum())
```

### ATAN2(y, x)

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/trigonometry.rst

Computes the four-quadrant inverse tangent of y/x in radians. It allows computing the angle for two given coordinate columns in Polars SQL.

```APIDOC
## ATAN2

### Description
Compute the inverse tangent of column_1/column_2 (in radians).

### Syntax
```sql
ATAN2(column_1, column_2)
```

### Parameters
- **column_1** (numeric) - The y-coordinate / numerator column.
- **column_2** (numeric) - The x-coordinate / denominator column.

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": [-2.0, -1.0, 1.0, 2.0],
        "b": [1.5, 1.0, 0.5, 0.0],
    }
)
df.sql("SELECT a, b, ATAN2(a, b) AS atan2_ab FROM self")
# shape: (4, 3)
# ┌──────┬─────┬───────────┐
# │ a    ┆ b   ┆ atan2_ab  │
# │ ---  ┆ --- ┆ ---       │
# │ f64  ┆ f64 ┆ f64       │
# ╞══════╪═════╪═══════════╡
# │ -2.0 ┆ 1.5 ┆ -0.927295 │
# │ -1.0 ┆ 1.0 ┆ -0.785398 │
# │ 1.0  ┆ 0.5 ┆ 1.107149  │
# │ 2.0  ┆ 0.0 ┆ 1.570796  │
# └──────┴─────┴───────────┘
```
```

### ARRAY_AGG

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/array.rst

Aggregates a column or expression into an array (equivalent to `implode`). Supports optional inline ORDER BY and LIMIT clauses.

```APIDOC
## ARRAY_AGG

### Description
Aggregate a column/expression as an array (equivalent to `implode`). Supports optional inline `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT` clauses.

### Syntax
```sql
ARRAY_AGG(expression [ORDER BY sort_expression [ASC | DESC]] [LIMIT n])
```

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": [1, 2, 3], "bar": [4, 5, 6]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    ARRAY_AGG(foo ORDER BY foo DESC) AS arr_foo,
    ARRAY_AGG(bar LIMIT 2) AS arr_bar
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌───────────┬───────────┐
# │ arr_foo   ┆ arr_bar   │
# │ ---       ┆ ---       │
# │ list[i64] ┆ list[i64] │
# ╞═══════════╪═══════════╡
# │ [3, 2, 1] ┆ [4, 5]    │
# └───────────┴───────────┘
```
```

### Compute array inner product with ARRAY_INNER_PRODUCT

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/array.rst

Calculate the dot product of two fixed-size arrays of equal width or between an array column and a literal array. Coordinates with null values do not contribute to the result, and null array rows return null.

```python
dtype = pl.Array(pl.Float64, 2)
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "lhs": [[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]],
        "rhs": [[10.0, 20.0], [30.0, 40.0]],
    },
    schema={"lhs": dtype, "rhs": dtype},
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT ARRAY_INNER_PRODUCT(lhs, rhs) AS dot FROM self
""")
# shape: (2, 1)
# ┌───────┐
# │ dot   │
# │ ---   │
# │ f64   │
# ╞═══════╡
# │ 50.0  │
# │ 250.0 │
# └───────┘

df.sql("""
  SELECT ARRAY_INNER_PRODUCT(lhs, [10.0, 20.0]) AS dot FROM self
""")
# shape: (2, 1)
# ┌───────┐
# │ dot   │
# │ ---   │
# │ f64   │
# ╞═══════╡
# │ 50.0  │
# │ 110.0 │
# └───────┘
```

### Filter with IN and NOT IN operators

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/operators/index.rst

Test membership in a list of values using IN and NOT IN within a Polars SQL query.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"n": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]})
df.sql("SELECT * FROM self WHERE n IN (2, 4)")
# shape: (2, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ n   │
# │ --- │
# │ i64 │
# ╞═════╡
# │ 2   │
# │ 4   │
# └─────┘

df.sql("SELECT * FROM self WHERE n NOT IN (2, 4)")
# shape: (3, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ n   │
# │ --- │
# │ i64 │
# ╞═════╡
# │ 1   │
# │ 3   │
# │ 5   │
# └─────┘
```

### Configure Cargo.toml for Polars Expression Plugin

[package]
name = "expression_lib"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

name = "expression_lib"
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
polars = { version = "*" }
pyo3 = { version = "*", features = ["extension-module", "abi3-py310"] }
pyo3-polars = { version = "*", features = ["derive"] }
serde = { version = "*", features = ["derive"] }
```

### Match regex patterns using REGEXP_LIKE in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Tests if a string column matches a given regular expression pattern and returns a boolean result.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["abc123", "4ab4a", "abc456", "321cba"]})
df.sql(r"""
  SELECT foo, REGEXP_LIKE(foo, '\d$') AS ends_in_digit FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 2)
# ┌────────┬───────────────┐
# │ foo    ┆ ends_in_digit │
# │ ---    ┆ ---           │
# │ str    ┆ bool          │
# ╞════════╪═══════════════╡
# │ abc123 ┆ true          │
# │ 4ab4a  ┆ false         │
# │ abc456 ┆ true          │

### Extract temporal parts using EXTRACT in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/temporal.rst

Extract date components such as decade, year, and quarter from date columns using the SQL EXTRACT function.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "dt": [
      date(1969, 12, 31),
      date(2026, 8, 22),
      date(2077, 2, 10),
    ],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    dt,
    EXTRACT(decade FROM dt) AS decade,
    EXTRACT(year FROM dt) AS year,
    EXTRACT(quarter FROM dt) AS quarter,
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (3, 4)
# ┌────────────┬────────┬──────┬─────────┐
# │ dt         ┆ decade ┆ year ┆ quarter │
# │ ---        ┆ ---    ┆ ---  ┆ ---     │
# │ date       ┆ i32    ┆ i32  ┆ i8      │
# ╞════════════╪════════╪══════╪═════════╡
# │ 1969-12-31 ┆ 196    ┆ 1969 ┆ 4       │
# │ 2026-08-22 ┆ 202    ┆ 2026 ┆ 3       │
# │ 2077-02-10 ┆ 207    ┆ 2077 ┆ 1       │
# └────────────┴────────┴──────┴─────────┘
```

### RPAD(string, length [, fill])

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Pads a string on the right to a specified length using an optional fill character. If the string exceeds the target length, it is truncated.

```APIDOC
## RPAD(string, length [, fill])

### Description
Pads a string on the right to a specified length using an optional fill character (default is a space). If the string is longer than the target length it is truncated.

### Syntax
```sql
RPAD(string, length [, fill])
```

### Parameters
- **string** (str) - The input string column or literal to pad.
- **length** (int) - The target length of the resulting string.
- **fill** (str, optional) - The character used to pad the string. Defaults to a space (`' '`).

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["hello", "hi", "a", None, "longstr"]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    foo,
    RPAD(foo, 7) AS rpad,
    RPAD(foo, 7, '-') AS rpad_dash,
    RPAD(foo, 4, '#') AS rpad_trunc
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (5, 4)
# ┌─────────┬─────────┬───────────┬────────────┐
# │ foo     ┆ rpad    ┆ rpad_dash ┆ rpad_trunc │
# │ ---     ┆ ---     ┆ ---       ┆ ---        │
# │ str     ┆ str     ┆ str       ┆ str        │
# ╞═════════╪═════════╪═══════════╪════════════╡
# │ hello   ┆ hello   ┆ hello--   ┆ hell       │
# │ hi      ┆ hi      ┆ hi-----   ┆ hi##       │
# │ a       ┆ a       ┆ a------   ┆ a###       │
# │ null    ┆ null    ┆ null      ┆ null       │
# │ longstr ┆ longstr ┆ longstr   ┆ long       │
# └─────────┴─────────┴───────────┴────────────┘
```
```

--------------------------------

### Strip characters from strings using TRIM in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Demonstrates stripping whitespace or specific characters from the left, right, or both sides of string columns using TRIM, TRIM(LEADING ...), and TRIM(TRAILING ...).

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["  hello  ", "  world  ", "  test  "]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    foo,
    TRIM(foo) AS trimmed,
    TRIM(LEADING ' ' FROM foo) AS ltrimmed,
    TRIM(TRAILING ' ' FROM foo) AS rtrimmed
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (3, 4)
# ┌───────────┬─────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
# │ foo       ┆ trimmed ┆ ltrimmed ┆ rtrimmed │
# │ ---       ┆ ---     ┆ ---      ┆ ---      │
# │ str       ┆ str     ┆ str      ┆ str      │
# ╞═══════════╪═════════╪══════════╪══════════╡
# │   hello   ┆ hello   ┆ hello    ┆   hello  │
# │   world   ┆ world   ┆ world    ┆   world  │
# │   test    ┆ test    ┆ test     ┆   test   │
# └───────────┴─────────┴──────────┴──────────┘
```

### Series.plot

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/series/plot.rst

Property that creates a plot namespace for a Polars Series, delegating plotting logic to Altair.

```APIDOC
## Property: Series.plot

### Description
Create a plot namespace. Polars delegates plotting logic to Altair.

*Warning: This functionality is currently considered unstable and may change without being considered a breaking change.*

### Type
`SeriesPlot`

### Methods Available on Namespace
- `s.plot.hist(**kwargs)`: Shorthand for generating an Altair binned histogram bar chart.
- `s.plot.kde(**kwargs)`: Shorthand for generating an Altair kernel density estimation (KDE) area plot.
- `s.plot.<attr>(**kwargs)`: Shorthand for generating an Altair chart using `mark_<attr>` (e.g., `s.plot.line()`).

### Examples
```python
import polars as pl

s = pl.Series([1, 4, 4, 6, 2, 4, 3, 5, 5, 7, 1])

# Histogram
s.plot.hist()

# KDE plot
s.plot.kde()

# Line plot
s.plot.line()
```

### Observe preserved height and ShapeError on zero-width DataFrame

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/releases/upgrade/2.md

Dropping all columns now retains the frame height rather than collapsing to (0, 0). Adding a column to an empty pl.DataFrame() raises ShapeError due to fixed length 0.

```pycon
>>> df.drop("*").shape
(3, 0)
>>> pl.DataFrame().with_columns(pl.Series([None, None]))
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
polars.exceptions.ShapeError: can't broadcast Series '' of length 2 to length 0
```

### ATAN2D(y, x)

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/trigonometry.rst

Computes the four-quadrant inverse tangent of y/x in degrees. This function is available for evaluating two-coordinate angles in Polars SQL queries.

```APIDOC
## ATAN2D

### Description
Compute the inverse tangent of column_1/column_2 (in degrees).

### Syntax
```sql
ATAN2D(column_1, column_2)
```

### Parameters
- **column_1** (numeric) - The y-coordinate / numerator column.
- **column_2** (numeric) - The x-coordinate / denominator column.

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0],
        "b": [1.0, 1.0, 0.0, -1.0],
    }
)
df.sql("SELECT a, b, ATAN2D(a, b) AS atan2d_ab FROM self")
# shape: (4, 3)
# ┌──────┬──────┬───────────┐
# │ a    ┆ b    ┆ atan2d_ab │
# │ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---       │
# │ f64  ┆ f64  ┆ f64       │
# ╞══════╪══════╪═══════════╡
# │ -1.0 ┆ 1.0  ┆ -45.0     │
# │ 0.0  ┆ 1.0  ┆ 0.0       │
# │ 1.0  ┆ 0.0  ┆ 90.0      │
# │ 1.0  ┆ -1.0 ┆ 135.0     │
# └──────┴──────┴───────────┘
```
```

### Aggregate columns into an array with ARRAY_AGG

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/array.rst

Aggregate a column or expression into an array (equivalent to implode). Supports optional inline ORDER BY and LIMIT clauses.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": [1, 2, 3], "bar": [4, 5, 6]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    ARRAY_AGG(foo ORDER BY foo DESC) AS arr_foo,
    ARRAY_AGG(bar LIMIT 2) AS arr_bar
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌───────────┬───────────┐
# │ arr_foo   ┆ arr_bar   │
# │ ---       ┆ ---       │
# │ list[i64] ┆ list[i64] │
# ╞═══════════╪═══════════╡
# │ [3, 2, 1] ┆ [4, 5]    │
# └───────────┴───────────┘
```

### Define dynamic output types using output_type_func and FieldsMapper

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/plugins/expr_plugins.md

Provide `output_type_func` to `#[polars_expr()]` to resolve output data types dynamically from input fields. Use `FieldsMapper` to map input fields to the corresponding float data type.

```rust
use polars_plan::dsl::FieldsMapper;

fn haversine_output(input_fields: &[Field]) -> PolarsResult<Field> {
    FieldsMapper::new(input_fields).map_to_float_dtype()
}

#[polars_expr(output_type_func=haversine_output)]
fn haversine(inputs: &[Series]) -> PolarsResult<Series> {
    let out = match inputs[0].dtype() {
        DataType::Float32 => {
            let start_lat = inputs[0].f32().unwrap();
            let start_long = inputs[1].f32().unwrap();
            let end_lat = inputs[2].f32().unwrap();
            let end_long = inputs[3].f32().unwrap();
            crate::distances::naive_haversine(start_lat, start_long, end_lat, end_long)?
                .into_series()
        }
        DataType::Float64 => {
            let start_lat = inputs[0].f64().unwrap();
            let start_long = inputs[1].f64().unwrap();
            let end_lat = inputs[2].f64().unwrap();
            let end_long = inputs[3].f64().unwrap();
            crate::distances::naive_haversine(start_lat, start_long, end_lat, end_long)?
                .into_series()
        }
        _ => polars_bail!(InvalidOperation: "only supported for float types"),
    };
    Ok(out)
}
```

### Find substring location using POSITION in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Returns the 1-indexed position of a substring within a string column, returning 0 if the substring is not found.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["apple", "banana", "orange", "grape"]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT foo, POSITION('an' IN foo) AS pos FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 2)
# ┌────────┬─────┐
# │ foo    ┆ pos │
# │ ---    ┆ --- │
# │ str    ┆ u32 │
# ╞════════╪═════╡
# │ apple  ┆ 0   │
# │ banana ┆ 2   │
# │ orange ┆ 3   │
# │ grape  ┆ 0   │
# └────────┴─────┘
```

### Format temporal values using STRFTIME in SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/temporal.rst

Formats Datetime, Date, or Time values into string format using chrono strftime-compatible format strings within a Polars SQL query.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "dt": [date(1978, 7, 5), None, date(2020, 4, 10)],
    "tm": [time(10, 10, 10), time(22, 33, 55), None],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    STRFTIME(dt, '%B %d, %Y') AS s_dt,
    STRFTIME(tm, '%H.%M.%S') AS s_tm,
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (3, 2)
# ┌────────────────┬──────────┐
# │ s_dt           ┆ s_tm     │
# │ ---            ┆ ---      │
# │ str            ┆ str      │
# ╞════════════════╪══════════╡
# │ July 05, 1978  ┆ 10.10.10 │
# │ null           ┆ 22.33.55 │
# │ April 10, 2020 ┆ null     │
# └────────────────┴──────────┘
```

### Filter with BETWEEN and NOT BETWEEN operators

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/operators/index.rst

# shape: (2, 1)

### Compute four-quadrant inverse tangent in radians using ATAN2

### Combine head and sum expressions in Polars

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/migration/spark.md

Combines independent head and sum operations within a single select context in Polars. The single scalar sum value is repeated across the output rows.

```python
df.select(
    pl.col("foo").sort().head(2),
    pl.col("bar").filter(pl.col("foo") == "d").sum()
)
```

```text
shape: (2, 2)

│ b   ┆ 9   │

```

### Define Rust expression plugin with kwargs struct

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/plugins/expr_plugins.md

Define a custom struct deriving serde::Deserialize as the second argument in a Polars expression plugin function.

```rust
/// Provide your own kwargs struct with the proper schema and accept that type
/// in your plugin expression.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct MyKwargs {
    float_arg: f64,
    integer_arg: i64,
    string_arg: String,
    boolean_arg: bool,
}

/// If you want to accept `kwargs`. You define a `kwargs` argument
/// on the second position in you plugin. You can provide any custom struct that is deserializable
/// with the pickle protocol (on the Rust side).
#[polars_expr(output_type=String)]
fn append_kwargs(input: &[Series], kwargs: MyKwargs) -> PolarsResult<Series> {
    let input = &input[0];
    let input = input.cast(&DataType::String)?;
    let ca = input.str().unwrap();

    Ok(ca
        .apply_into_string_amortized(|val, buf| {
            write!(
                buf,
                "{}-{}-{}-{}-{}",
                val, kwargs.float_arg, kwargs.integer_arg, kwargs.string_arg, kwargs.boolean_arg
            )
                .unwrap()
        })
        .into_series())
}
```

### Register custom LazyFrame namespace with register_lazyframe_namespace

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/api.rst

Registers a custom namespace on LazyFrame objects to perform custom operations, such as upcasting integer column types.

```python
@pl.api.register_lazyframe_namespace("types")
class DTypeOperations:
    def __init__(self, ldf: pl.LazyFrame) -> None:
        self._ldf = ldf

    def upcast_integer_types(self) -> pl.LazyFrame:
        return self._ldf.with_columns(
            pl.col(tp).cast(pl.Int64)
            for tp in (pl.Int8, pl.Int16, pl.Int32)
        )


ldf = pl.DataFrame(
    data={"a": [1, 2], "b": [3, 4], "c": [5.6, 6.7]},
    schema=[("a", pl.Int16), ("b", pl.Int32), ("c", pl.Float32)],
).lazy()

ldf.types.upcast_integer_types()

# shape: (2, 3)          shape: (2, 3)
# ┌─────┬─────┬─────┐    ┌─────┬─────┬─────┐
# │ a   ┆ b   ┆ c   │    │ a   ┆ b   ┆ c   │
# │ --- ┆ --- ┆ --- │    │ --- ┆ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i16 ┆ i32 ┆ f32 │ >> │ i64 ┆ i64 ┆ f32 │
# ╞═════╪═════╪═════╡    ╞═════╪═════╪═════╡
# │ 1   ┆ 3   ┆ 5.6 │    │ 1   ┆ 3   ┆ 5.6 │
# │ 2   ┆ 4   ┆ 6.7 │    │ 2   ┆ 4   ┆ 6.7 │
# └─────┴─────┴─────┘    └─────┴─────┴─────┘
```

### Perform set operations on selectors

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/selectors.rst

Combine selectors using set operations like union (`|`), intersection (`&`), difference (`-`), symmetric difference (`^`), and complement (`~`). Matching columns are consistently returned in the frame schema's original order.

```python
import polars.selectors as cs
import polars as pl

# set up an empty dataframe with plenty of columns of various dtypes
df = pl.DataFrame(
schema={
    "abc": pl.UInt16,
    "bbb": pl.UInt32,
    "cde": pl.Float64,
    "def": pl.Float32,
    "eee": pl.Boolean,
    "fgg": pl.Boolean,
    "ghi": pl.Time,
    "JJK": pl.Date,
    "Lmn": pl.Duration,
    "opp": pl.Datetime("ms"),
    "qqR": pl.String,
},
)

# Select the UNION of temporal, strings and columns that start with "e"
assert df.select(cs.temporal() | cs.string() | cs.starts_with("e")).schema == {
    "eee": pl.Boolean,
    "ghi": pl.Time,
    "JJK": pl.Date,
    "Lmn": pl.Duration,
    "opp": pl.Datetime("ms"),
    "qqR": pl.String,
}

# Select the INTERSECTION of temporal and column names that match "opp" OR "JJK"
assert df.select(cs.temporal() & cs.matches("opp|JJK")).schema == {
    "JJK": pl.Date,
    "opp": pl.Datetime("ms"),
}

# Select the DIFFERENCE of temporal columns and columns that contain the name "opp" OR "JJK"
assert df.select(cs.temporal() - cs.matches("opp|JJK")).schema == {
    "ghi": pl.Time,
    "Lmn": pl.Duration,
}

# Select the SYMMETRIC DIFFERENCE of numeric columns and columns that contain an "e"
assert df.select(cs.contains("e") ^ cs.numeric()).schema == {
    "abc": UInt16,
    "bbb": UInt32,
    "eee": Boolean,
}

# Select the COMPLEMENT of all columns of dtypes Duration and Time
assert df.select(~cs.by_dtype([pl.Duration, pl.Time])).schema == {
    "abc": pl.UInt16,
    "bbb": pl.UInt32,
    "cde": pl.Float64,
    "def": pl.Float32,
    "eee": pl.Boolean,
    "fgg": pl.Boolean,
    "JJK": pl.Date,
    "opp": pl.Datetime("ms"),
    "qqR": pl.String,
}
```

### ARRAY_INNER_PRODUCT

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/array.rst

Returns the inner product of two fixed-size arrays of equal width. Elements are cast to a common integer or float supertype. ARRAY_DOT_PRODUCT is supported as an alias.

```APIDOC
## ARRAY_INNER_PRODUCT

### Description
Returns the inner product of two fixed-size arrays of equal width. Their inner data types are cast to a common supertype, which must be an integer, `Float32`, or `Float64`. `ARRAY_DOT_PRODUCT` is an alias.

Inputs may be fixed-size Array expressions or direct, known-width SQL array literals. Direct literals are interpreted as scalar fixed-size Arrays and broadcast against the other input. Variable-size List dtypes are not implicitly converted.

Coordinates where either array element is null do not contribute to the result. A non-null row with no valid coordinate pairs returns zero. If either input Array is null for a row, the result for that row is null.

### Syntax
```sql
ARRAY_INNER_PRODUCT(lhs, rhs)
ARRAY_DOT_PRODUCT(lhs, rhs)
```

### Parameters
- **lhs** (Array) - Left-hand side fixed-size array expression or array literal.
- **rhs** (Array) - Right-hand side fixed-size array expression or array literal of equal width.

### Example
```python
dtype = pl.Array(pl.Float64, 2)
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "lhs": [[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]],
        "rhs": [[10.0, 20.0], [30.0, 40.0]],
    },
    schema={"lhs": dtype, "rhs": dtype},
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT ARRAY_INNER_PRODUCT(lhs, rhs) AS dot FROM self
""")
# shape: (2, 1)
# ┌───────┐
# │ dot   │
# │ ---   │
# │ f64   │
# ╞═══════╡
# │ 50.0  │
# │ 250.0 │
# └───────┘

df.sql("""
  SELECT ARRAY_INNER_PRODUCT(lhs, [10.0, 20.0]) AS dot FROM self
""")
# shape: (2, 1)
# ┌───────┐
# │ dot   │
# │ ---   │
# │ f64   │
# ╞═══════╡
# │ 50.0  │
# │ 110.0 │
# └───────┘
```
```

### TRIM

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Strips whitespace or specified characters from the left, right, or both sides of a string expression. Supports standard SQL TRIM syntax variants including LEADING, TRAILING, and BOTH.

```APIDOC
### TRIM

Strips characters from the left and/or right of a string.

#### Syntax
* `TRIM(expr)` - strip whitespace from both sides.
* `TRIM(BOTH char FROM expr)` - strip `char` from both sides.
* `TRIM(LEADING char FROM expr)` - strip `char` from the left.
* `TRIM(TRAILING char FROM expr)` - strip `char` from the right.

#### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["  hello  ", "  world  ", "  test  "]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    foo,
    TRIM(foo) AS trimmed,
    TRIM(LEADING ' ' FROM foo) AS ltrimmed,
    TRIM(TRAILING ' ' FROM foo) AS rtrimmed
  FROM self
""")
```
```

### Calculate group size using pandas groupby transform

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/migration/pandas.md

Groups by column 'c', computes the group length on column 'type', and joins the result back as a new column.

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "c": [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2],
    "type": ["m", "n", "o", "m", "m", "n", "n"],
})

df["size"] = df.groupby("c")["type"].transform(len)
```

```text
   c type size
0  1    m    3
1  1    n    3
2  1    o    3
3  2    m    4
4  2    m    4
5  2    n    4
6  2    n    4
```

### Install Polars for Rust

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/getting-started.md

Add Polars with lazy evaluation features enabled to a Rust project via cargo command line or Cargo.toml.

```shell
cargo add polars -F lazy

### OCTET_LENGTH

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Returns the length of a given string in bytes.

```APIDOC
## OCTET_LENGTH

### Description
Returns the length of a given string in bytes.

### Syntax
```sql
OCTET_LENGTH(string)
```

### Parameters
- **string** (str) - The input string column to measure.

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "iso_lang": ["de", "ru", "es"],
    "color": ["weiß", "синий", "amarillo"],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    iso_lang,
    color,
    OCTET_LENGTH(color) AS n_bytes,
    LENGTH(color) AS n_chars
  FROM self
""")
```
```

### AssertionError from unmaterialized branching LazyFrames

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/lazy/multiplexing.md

Output error that occurs when branching from an unmaterialized LazyFrame. Re-evaluating an unstable operation like group_by on separate collections produces differing row orders.

```python
AssertionError: DataFrames are different (value mismatch for column 'n')
[left]:  [9, 2, 0, 5, 3, 1, 7, 8, 6, 4]
[right]: [0, 9, 6, 8, 2, 5, 4, 3, 1, 7]
```

### Evaluate smallest value using LEAST in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/conditional.rst

Returns the smallest value from a list of expressions evaluated row-wise in a SQL query.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": [100, 200, 300, 400],
    "bar": [20, 10, 30, 40]
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT LEAST(foo, bar) AS baz FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 1)
# ┌─────┐
# │ baz │
# │ --- │
# │ i64 │
# ╞═════╡
# │ 20  │
# │ 10  │
# │ 30  │
# │ 40  │
# └─────┘
```

### Left-pad strings with LPAD

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Pads a string on the left to a target length using spaces by default or a custom fill character. Truncates the string if it exceeds the specified target length.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["hello", "hi", "a", None, "longstr"]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    foo,
    LPAD(foo, 7) AS lpad,
    LPAD(foo, 7, 'x') AS lpad_x,
    LPAD(foo, 4, '#') AS lpad_trunc
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (5, 4)
# ┌─────────┬─────────┬─────────┬────────────┐
# │ foo     ┆ lpad    ┆ lpad_x  ┆ lpad_trunc │
# │ ---     ┆ ---     ┆ ---     ┆ ---        │
# │ str     ┆ str     ┆ str     ┆ str        │
# ╞═════════╪═════════╪═════════╪════════════╡
# │ hello   ┆   hello ┆ xxhello ┆ hell       │
# │ hi      ┆      hi ┆ xxxxxhi ┆ ##hi       │
# │ a       ┆       a ┆ xxxxxxa ┆ ###a       │
# │ null    ┆ null    ┆ null    ┆ null       │
# │ longstr ┆ longstr ┆ longstr ┆ long       │
# └─────────┴─────────┴─────────┴────────────┘
```

### Strip trailing whitespace using RTRIM in SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Strips whitespace characters from the right end of a string column.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"bar": ["zz    ", "yy  ", "xx ", "ww   "]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT bar, RTRIM(bar) AS baz FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 2)
# ┌────────┬─────┐
# │ bar    ┆ baz │
# │ ---    ┆ --- │
# │ str    ┆ str │
# ╞════════╪═════╡
# │ zz     ┆ zz  │
# │ yy     ┆ yy  │
# │ xx     ┆ xx  │
# │ ww     ┆ ww  │
# └────────┴─────┘
```

### Convert datatypes using CAST or shorthand syntax

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/types.rst

Convert values to specified datatypes in a SQL query. Supports PostgreSQL-style `<expr>::type` syntax in addition to standard `CAST`.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": [20, 10, 30],
    "bar": ["1999-12-31", "2012-07-05", "2024-01-01"],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    foo::float4,
    bar::date
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (3, 2)
# ┌──────┬────────────┐
# │ foo  ┆ bar        │
# │ ---  ┆ ---        │
# │ f32  ┆ date       │
# ╞══════╪════════════╡
# │ 20.0 ┆ 1999-12-31 │
# │ 10.0 ┆ 2012-07-05 │
# │ 30.0 ┆ 2024-01-01 │
# └──────┴────────────┘
```

### Register Polars Plugin Function in Python

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/plugins/expr_plugins.md

Registers the compiled Rust plugin function using register_plugin_function and marks it as elementwise for batch processing.

```python
# expression_lib/__init__.py
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import polars as pl
from polars.plugins import register_plugin_function
from polars._typing import IntoExpr

PLUGIN_PATH = Path(__file__).parent

def pig_latinnify(expr: IntoExpr) -> pl.Expr:
    """Pig-latinnify expression."""
    return register_plugin_function(
        plugin_path=PLUGIN_PATH,
        function_name="pig_latinnify",
        args=expr,
        is_elementwise=True,
    )
```

### Limit returned rows with LIMIT clause

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/clauses.rst

Limit the maximum number of rows returned by a query.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "foo": ["b", "a", "c", "b"],
    "bar": [20, 10, 40, 30],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT foo, bar FROM self LIMIT 2
""")
# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ foo ┆ bar │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ str ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ b   ┆ 20  │
# │ a   ┆ 10  │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### Select columns using SELECT

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/clauses.rst

Selects specific columns to return from a DataFrame via the `sql` method. Using bare `FROM tbl` is also supported as shorthand for `SELECT * FROM tbl`.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "a": [1, 2, 3],
    "b": ["zz", "yy", "xx"],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT a, b FROM self
""")
# shape: (3, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ a   ┆ b   │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ str │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 1   ┆ zz  │
# │ 2   ┆ yy  │
# │ 3   ┆ xx  │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### Implement Pig Latin Expression in Rust with polars_expr

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/plugins/expr_plugins.md

Exposes a custom expression function using the #[polars_expr] attribute and processes string chunks elementwise with amortized string allocation.

```rust
// src/expressions.rs
use polars::prelude::*;
use pyo3_polars::derive::polars_expr;
use std::fmt::Write;

fn pig_latin_str(value: &str, output: &mut String) {
    if let Some(first_char) = value.chars().next() {
        write!(output, "{}{}", &value[1..], first_char).unwrap()
    }
}

#[polars_expr(output_type=String)]
fn pig_latinnify(inputs: &[Series]) -> PolarsResult<Series> {
    let ca = inputs[0].str()?;
    let out: StringChunked = ca.apply_into_string_amortized(pig_latin_str);
    Ok(out.into_series())
}
```

### STRFTIME(temporal_value, format)

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/temporal.rst

Formats a temporal value (Datetime, Date, or Time) as a string using a chrono strftime-compatible format string in Polars SQL.

```APIDOC
## STRFTIME

### Description
Formats a temporal value (Datetime, Date, or Time) as a string using a chrono strftime-compatible formatting string.

### Syntax
```sql
STRFTIME(temporal_value, format)
```

### Parameters
- **temporal_value** (*Datetime*, *Date*, or *Time*) - The temporal column or value to format.
- **format** (*string*) - A format string compatible with chrono strftime.

### Example
```python
import polars as pl
from datetime import date, time

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "dt": [date(1978, 7, 5), None, date(2020, 4, 10)],
        "tm": [time(10, 10, 10), time(22, 33, 55), None],
    }
)

df.sql("""
    SELECT
        STRFTIME(dt, '%B %d, %Y') AS s_dt,
        STRFTIME(tm, '%H.%M.%S') AS s_tm,
    FROM self
""")
```

### Output
```text
shape: (3, 2)
┌────────────────┬──────────┐
│ s_dt           ┆ s_tm     │
│ ---            ┆ ---      │
│ str            ┆ str      │
╞════════════════╪══════════╡
│ July 05, 1978  ┆ 10.10.10 │
│ null           ┆ 22.33.55 │
│ April 10, 2020 ┆ null     │
└────────────────┴──────────┘
```
```

### Register plugin function with Python

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/pyo3-polars/README.md

Exposes the compiled Rust expression to Python using register_plugin_function with elementwise processing enabled.

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import polars as pl
from polars.plugins import register_plugin_function

from expression_lib._utils import LIB

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from expression_lib._typing import IntoExprColumn


def pig_latinnify(expr: IntoExprColumn, capitalize: bool = False) -> pl.Expr:
    return register_plugin_function(
        plugin_path=LIB,
        args=[expr],
        function_name="pig_latinnify",
        is_elementwise=True,
        kwargs={"capitalize": capitalize},
    )
```

### Substitute occurrences of a substring using REPLACE in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

# │ foo    ┆ bar    │
# │ ---    ┆ ---    │
# │ str    ┆ str    │

### Split strings by delimiter using SPLIT_PART in SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Splits a string by a substring or delimiter and retrieves the specified 1-indexed n-th part, supporting negative indices from the end.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"s": ["xx,yy,zz", "abc,,xyz,???,hmm", None, ""]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    s,
    SPLIT_PART(s,',',1) AS "s+1",
    SPLIT_PART(s,',',3) AS "s+3",
    SPLIT_PART(s,',',-2) AS "s-2",
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 4)
# ┌──────────────────┬──────┬──────┬──────┐
# │ s                ┆ s+1  ┆ s+3  ┆ s-2  │
# │ ---              ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---  │
# │ str              ┆ str  ┆ str  ┆ str  │
# ╞══════════════════╪══════╪══════╪══════╡
# │ xx,yy,zz         ┆ xx   ┆ zz   ┆ yy   │
# │ abc,,xyz,???,hmm ┆ abc  ┆ xyz  ┆ ???  │
# │ null             ┆ null ┆ null ┆ null │
# │                  ┆      ┆      ┆      │
# └──────────────────┴──────┴──────┴──────┘
```

### STRPTIME(string, format)

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Converts a string to a Datetime using a chrono strftime-compatible formatting string.

```APIDOC
## STRPTIME

### Description
Converts a string to a Datetime using a chrono strftime-compatible formatting string.

### Syntax
```sql
STRPTIME(string, format)
```

### Parameters
- **string** (str) - The string to parse into a datetime.
- **format** (str) - The format string compatible with chrono strftime.

### Return Type
`datetime[μs]`

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "s_dt": ["1969 Oct 30", "2024 Jul 05", "2077 Feb 28"],
    "s_tm": ["00.30.55", "12.40.15", "10.45.00"],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    s_dt,
    s_tm,
    STRPTIME(s_dt || ' ' || s_tm, '%Y %b %d %H.%M.%S') AS dtm
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (3, 3)
# ┌─────────────┬──────────┬─────────────────────┐
# │ s_dt        ┆ s_tm     ┆ dtm                 │
# │ ---         ┆ ---      ┆ ---                 │
# │ str         ┆ str      ┆ datetime[μs]        │
# ╞═════════════╪══════════╪═════════════════════╡
# │ 1969 Oct 30 ┆ 00.30.55 ┆ 1969-10-30 00:30:55 │
# │ 2024 Jul 05 ┆ 12.40.15 ┆ 2024-07-05 12:40:15 │
# │ 2077 Feb 28 ┆ 10.45.00 ┆ 2077-02-28 10:45:00 │
# └─────────────┴──────────┴─────────────────────┘
```
```

### Convert strings to datetime using STRPTIME

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Converts string columns to Datetime using a chrono strftime-compatible format string.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
  {
    "s_dt": ["1969 Oct 30", "2024 Jul 05", "2077 Feb 28"],
    "s_tm": ["00.30.55", "12.40.15", "10.45.00"],
  }
)
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    s_dt,
    s_tm,
    STRPTIME(s_dt || ' ' || s_tm, '%Y %b %d %H.%M.%S') AS dtm
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (3, 3)
# ┌─────────────┬──────────┬─────────────────────┐
# │ s_dt        ┆ s_tm     ┆ dtm                 │
# │ ---         ┆ ---      ┆ ---                 │
# │ str         ┆ str      ┆ datetime[μs]        │
# ╞═════════════╪══════════╪═════════════════════╡
# │ 1969 Oct 30 ┆ 00.30.55 ┆ 1969-10-30 00:30:55 │
# │ 2024 Jul 05 ┆ 12.40.15 ┆ 2024-07-05 12:40:15 │
# │ 2077 Feb 28 ┆ 10.45.00 ┆ 2077-02-28 10:45:00 │
# └─────────────┴──────────┴─────────────────────┘
```

### Truncate Numbers Using TRUNC

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/math.rst

Truncate a number toward zero to a specified number of decimals (default is 0).

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.5671, -2.999, 3.4569, -4.3218]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT x, TRUNC(x) AS xt0, TRUNC(x, 2) AS xt2 FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 3)
# ┌─────────┬──────┬───────┐
# │ x       ┆ xt0  ┆ xt2   │
# │ ---     ┆ ---  ┆ ---   │
# │ f64     ┆ f64  ┆ f64   │
# ╞═════════╪══════╪═══════╡
# │ 1.5671  ┆ 1.0  ┆ 1.56  │
# │ -2.999  ┆ -2.0 ┆ -2.99 │
# │ 3.4569  ┆ 3.0  ┆ 3.45  │
# │ -4.3218 ┆ -4.0 ┆ -4.32 │
# └─────────┴──────┴───────┘
```

### Configure launch.json for dual Python and Rust debugging

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/development/contributing/ide.md

Add these configurations to `.vscode/launch.json` to enable simultaneous Python (`debugpy`) and Rust (`lldb`) debugging.

```json
{
  "configurations": [
    {
      "name": "Debug Rust/Python",
      "type": "debugpy",
      "request": "launch",
      "program": "${workspaceFolder}/py-polars/debug/launch.py",
      "args": [
        "${file}"
      ],
      "console": "internalConsole",
      "justMyCode": true,
      "serverReadyAction": {
        "pattern": "pID = ([0-9]+)",
        "action": "startDebugging",
        "name": "Rust LLDB"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "Rust LLDB",
      "pid": "0",
      "type": "lldb",
      "request": "attach",
      "program": "${workspaceFolder}/py-polars/.venv/bin/python",
      "stopOnEntry": false,
      "sourceLanguages": [
        "rust"
      ],
      "presentation": {
        "hidden": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Define parse_schema for CSV header

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/docs/source/user-guide/plugins/io_plugins.md

Extracts column names from the first line of a CSV string and constructs a Polars schema with String columns.

```python
def parse_schema(csv_str: str) -> pl.Schema:
    first_line = csv_str.split("\n")[0]

    return pl.Schema({k: pl.String for k in first_line.split(",")})
```

### REVERSE(string)

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Reverses the characters in a given string. Useful for string manipulation within SQL queries executed on Polars DataFrames.

```APIDOC
## REVERSE(string)

### Description
Returns the reversed string.

### Syntax
```sql
REVERSE(string)
```

### Parameters
- **string** (str) - The input string column or literal to reverse.

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["apple", "banana", "orange", "grape"]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT foo, REVERSE(foo) AS oof FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 2)
# ┌────────┬────────┐
# │ foo    ┆ oof    │
# │ ---    ┆ ---    │
# │ str    ┆ str    │
# ╞════════╪════════╡
# │ apple  ┆ elppa  │
# │ banana ┆ ananab │
# │ orange ┆ egnaro │
# │ grape  ┆ eparg  │
# └────────┴────────┘
```
```

### EXTRACT(field FROM source)

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/temporal.rst

Extracts a specific part or component (such as year, month, or day) from a date or datetime value in Polars SQL queries. Supported parts return corresponding numeric or time data types.

```APIDOC
## EXTRACT(field FROM source)

### Description
Extracts a part of a date (or datetime) such as ‘year’, ‘month’, etc.

### Syntax
`EXTRACT(part FROM date_or_datetime_expression)`

### Supported Parts and Return Types
| Part | Description | DataType |
|---|---|---|
| ‘millennium’, ‘millennia’ | Millennium number | Int32 |
| ‘century’, ‘centuries’, ‘c’ | Century number | Int32 |
| ‘decade’, ‘decades’ | Decade number (year / 10) | Int32 |
| ‘isoyear’ | ISO year number | Int32 |
| ‘year’, ‘years’, ‘y’ | Calendar year | Int32 |
| ‘quarter’, ‘quarters’ | Quarter of the year (1–4) | Int8 |
| ‘month’, ‘months’, ‘mon’, ‘mons’ | Month of the year (1–12) | Int8 |
| ‘dayofyear’, ‘doy’ | Day of the year (1–366) | Int16 |
| ‘dayofweek’, ‘dow’, ‘weekday’ | Day of the week (0:Sunday – 6:Saturday) | Int8 |
| ‘isoweek’, ‘week’ | ISO week number (1–53) | Int8 |
| ‘isodow’ | ISO day of the week (1:Monday – 7:Sunday) | Int8 |
| ‘day’, ‘days’, ‘dayofmonth’, d’ | Day of the month (1–31) | Int8 |
| ‘hour’, ‘hours’, ‘h’ | Hour of the day (0–23) | Int8 |
| ‘minute’, ‘minutes’, ‘mins’, ‘min’, ‘m’ | Minute of the hour (0–59) | Int8 |
| ‘second’, ‘seconds’, ‘sec’, ‘secs’, ‘s’ | Second of the minute (0–59) | Int8 |
| ‘millisecond’, ‘milliseconds’, ‘ms’ | Sub-minute seconds and milliseconds (0–59999.) | Float64 |
| ‘microsecond’, ‘microseconds’, ‘us’ | Sub-minute seconds and microseconds (0–59999999.) | Float64 |
| ‘nanosecond’, ‘nanoseconds’, ‘ns’ | Sub-minute seconds and nanoseconds (0–59999999999.) | Float64 |
| ‘timezone’ | UTC offset of the timezone, in seconds () | Int64 |
| ‘time’ | Time component | Time |
| ‘epoch’ | Seconds since Unix epoch (1970-01-01) | Float64 |

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "dt": [
            date(1969, 12, 31),
            date(2026, 8, 22),
            date(2077, 2, 10),
        ],
    }
)
df.sql("""
    SELECT
      dt,
      EXTRACT(decade FROM dt) AS decade,
      EXTRACT(year FROM dt) AS year,
      EXTRACT(quarter FROM dt) AS quarter,
    FROM self
""")
```
```

### Round numbers using ROUND in Polars SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/math.rst

Round a number to a specified number of decimal places (default is 0) away from zero.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"x": [-0.45, -1.81, 2.25, 3.99]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT x, ROUND(x) AS x_round, ROUND(x, 1) AS x_round_1 FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 3)
# ┌───────┬─────────┬───────────┐
# │ x     ┆ x_round ┆ x_round_1 │
# │ ---   ┆ ---     ┆ ---       │
# │ f64   ┆ f64     ┆ f64       │
# ╞═══════╪═════════╪═══════════╡
# │ -0.45 ┆ -0.0    ┆ -0.5      │
# │ -1.81 ┆ -2.0    ┆ -1.8      │
# │ 2.25  ┆ 2.0     ┆ 2.3       │
# │ 3.99  ┆ 4.0     ┆ 4.0       │
# └───────┴─────────┴───────────┘
```

### Right-pad strings with RPAD

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Pads a string on the right to a specified length using an optional fill character (defaulting to space). Truncates the string if it is longer than the target length.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["hello", "hi", "a", None, "longstr"]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    foo,
    RPAD(foo, 7) AS rpad,
    RPAD(foo, 7, '-') AS rpad_dash,
    RPAD(foo, 4, '#') AS rpad_trunc
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (5, 4)
# ┌─────────┬─────────┬───────────┬────────────┐
# │ foo     ┆ rpad    ┆ rpad_dash ┆ rpad_trunc │
# │ ---     ┆ ---     ┆ ---       ┆ ---        │
# │ str     ┆ str     ┆ str       ┆ str        │
# ╞═════════╪═════════╪═══════════╪════════════╡
# │ hello   ┆ hello   ┆ hello--   ┆ hell       │
# │ hi      ┆ hi      ┆ hi-----   ┆ hi##       │
# │ a       ┆ a       ┆ a------   ┆ a###       │
# │ null    ┆ null    ┆ null      ┆ null       │
# │ longstr ┆ longstr ┆ longstr   ┆ long       │
# └─────────┴─────────┴───────────┴────────────┘
```

### Count set bits using BIT_COUNT

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/bitwise.rst

Returns the number of bits set to 1 in the binary representation of integer column values using BIT_COUNT.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"i": [16, 10, 55, 127]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT
    i,
    BIT_COUNT(i) AS i_bitcount
  FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 2)
# ┌─────┬────────────┐
# │ i   ┆ i_bitcount │
# │ --- ┆ ---        │
# │ i64 ┆ u32        │
# ╞═════╪════════════╡
# │ 16  ┆ 1          │
# │ 10  ┆ 2          │
# │ 55  ┆ 5          │
# │ 127 ┆ 7          │
# └─────┴────────────┘
```

### Check string prefix with STARTS_WITH in SQL

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Returns true if the string value starts with the specified prefix substring, and false otherwise.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"foo": ["apple", "banana", "avocado", "grape"]})
df.sql("""
  SELECT foo, STARTS_WITH(foo, 'a') AS starts_a FROM self
""")
# shape: (4, 2)
# ┌─────────┬──────────┐
# │ foo     ┆ starts_a │
# │ ---     ┆ ---      │
# │ str     ┆ bool     │
# ╞═════════╪══════════╡
# │ apple   ┆ true     │
# │ banana  ┆ false    │
# │ avocado ┆ true     │
# │ grape   ┆ false    │
# └─────────┴──────────┘
```

### NORMALIZE

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/functions/string.rst

Converts a string to a specified Unicode normalization form (NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD).

```APIDOC
## NORMALIZE

### Description
Convert string to the specified Unicode normalization form (one of NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD). If the normalization form is not provided, NFC is used by default.

### Syntax
```sql
NORMALIZE(string[, form])
```

### Parameters
- **string** (str) - The input string to normalize.
- **form** (keyword/identifier, optional) - Normalization form: `NFC`, `NFD`, `NFKC`, or `NFKD`. Defaults to `NFC`.

### Example
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({
    "txt": [
        "Ｔｅｓｔ",
        "Ⓣⓔⓢⓣ",
        "𝕿𝖊𝖘𝖙",
        "𝕋𝕖𝖘𝖙",
        "𝗧𝖊𝖘𝖙",
    ],
})
df.sql("""
  SELECT NORMALIZE(txt, NFKC) FROM self
""").to_series()
```
```

### Use Config instance as a decorator

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/config.rst

Applies configuration options temporarily for the duration of a function call by setting apply_on_context_enter=True on the Config instance.

```python
cfg_ascii_frames = pl.Config(ascii_tables=True, apply_on_context_enter=True)

@cfg_ascii_frames
def write_markdown_frame_to_stdout(df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
    sys.stdout.write(str(df))
```

### Match regex case-insensitively using ~* and !~* operators

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/operators/index.rst

Use `~*` for case-insensitive regular expression matching and `!~*` for case-insensitive non-matching.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"idx": [0, 1, 2, 3], "lbl": ["FOO", "bar", "Baz", "ZAP"]})
df.sql("SELECT * FROM self WHERE lbl ~* '.*[aeiou]$'")
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ idx ┆ lbl │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ str │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 0   ┆ FOO │
# └─────┴─────┘

df.sql("SELECT * FROM self WHERE lbl !~* '^b[aeiou]'")
# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ idx ┆ lbl │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ str │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 0   ┆ FOO │
# │ 3   ┆ ZAP │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### Compare values across columns with ANY operator

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/sql/operators/index.rst

Compare a column value against any value in a column expression using the ANY operator. Supported comparison operators include >, <, >=, <=, =, and !=.

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 5, 10], "b": [3, 7, 3]})
df.sql("SELECT * FROM self WHERE a < ANY(b)")
# shape: (2, 2)
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ a   ┆ b   │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 1   ┆ 3   │
# │ 5   ┆ 7   │
# └─────┴─────┘
```

### Register custom DataFrame namespace with register_dataframe_namespace

Source: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/main/py-polars/docs/source/reference/api.rst

Registers a custom namespace on DataFrame objects to extend DataFrame functionality, such as splitting alternate rows.

```python
@pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("split")
class SplitFrame:
    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        self._df = df

    def by_alternate_rows(self) -> list[pl.DataFrame]:
        df = self._df.with_row_index(name="n")
        return [
            df.filter((pl.col("n") % 2) == 0).drop("n"),
            df.filter((pl.col("n") % 2) != 0).drop("n"),
        ]


pl.DataFrame(
    data=["aaa", "bbb", "ccc", "ddd", "eee", "fff"],
    schema=[("txt", pl.String)],
).split.by_alternate_rows()

# [┌─────┐  ┌─────┐
#  │ txt │  │ txt │
#  │ --- │  │ --- │
#  │ str │  │ str │
#  ╞═════╡  ╞═════╡
#  │ aaa │  │ bbb │
#  │ ccc │  │ ddd │
#  │ eee │  │ fff │
#  └─────┘, └─────┘]
```
